parts.text: A student investigates the balancing of a metre rule. Fig. 3.1 shows the set-up. Fig. 3.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The student places the metre rule on the pivot so that the metre rule is as near as possible to being balanced. Fig. 3.2 shows the position of the pivot. Fig. 3.2 Record the scale reading S on the metre rule at the point where the rule balances on the pivot. S = ................................................... cm [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) • The student places an object Q with its centre on the metre rule at the 90.0 cm mark. The position of Q is not changed during the experiment. • He places a load P of weight P = 1.0 N on the metre rule. • He adjusts the position of load P so that the metre rule is as near as possible to being balanced with the pivot directly below the scale reading S . • He records, in Table 3.1, the distance a from the centre of load P to the centre of load Q. • He repeats the procedure using loads of weight P = 2.0 N, 3.0 N, 4.0 N and 5.0 N. • He records all the values of a in Table 3.1. Complete the column headings in Table 3.1 by inserting the unit in the 1 P column. Table 3.1 P / N a / cm 1 P / 1.0 80.0 1.00 2.0 59.5 0.50 3.0 54.5 0.33 4.0 50.4 0.25 5.0 47.8 0.20 [1]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Plot a graph of a / cm ( y -axis) against 1 P ( x -axis). Start the y -axis at a / cm = 30. [4]

ms.label: 3(d)
ms.text:
axes correctly labelled with quantity and unit and correct way round
suitable scales with a axis starting from 30
all plots correct to ½ small square
good line judgement with thin continuous line

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = ......................................................... [3]

ms.label: 3(e)
ms.text:
triangle method clearly shown on graph
(triangle) covering at least ½ of candidate’s line between the extreme plots
G = 40.0 ± 1.0 (i.e. any answer between 39.0 and 41.0 inclusive)

parts.label: f
parts.text: (f) The gradient G is numerically equal to the distance d between the pivot and the centre of load Q. Record the value of d to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment. d = ................................................... cm [1]

ms.label: 3(f)
ms.text: d = G and given to 2 or 3 significant figures
